title: Trillion tokens, trillion parameters
gist: How Modal tuned its shared Kimi K2.6 service for coding-agent traffic, sold directly and through OpenRouter: a drafter first trained on a generic mix, then fine-tuned on coding traces the target model produced, an 8-bit KV cache, a CPU-memory cache tier, and load-aware session routing.
changes: A clean tuned-against-generic number at the level of the workload class: fine-tuning the drafter on the target model's own coding traces was worth about 20%. Modal says it then repeated the recipe, faster, for other models.
caveats: Opened first-hand on 21 Nov. Nothing says the drafter saw one customer's traffic; it can keep training on production outputs, but the 20% is on representative traces. The recipe carried over to other models, not customers. The 2.8x and 5.6x headline figures are against an unoptimised replica.

numbers.metric: Speculative accept length after fine-tuning the draft on coding traces for the target model
numbers.value: 5.00 to 5.84 tokens per step, about 20% faster

bears_on.note: Tuning a drafter to the coding-agent class, on the model's own outputs, was worth about 20%. This is class-level, not per-customer, tuning.
The stack was designed around the shape of coding-agent traffic: 100k tokens in, 500 out.
A drafter fine-tuned on the target model's coding traces accepted about 20% more tokens per step than a generic one.
